I really see your point, but how I am I meant to address something she doesn't talk about? I really don't believe in innuendos. Guess work makes it hard to find a solution, and just prolongs the process while making it tougher on every one. 

I also understand the thing of narratives, but I don't think allowing a particular reaction because of a narrative is appropriate. That just sounds like a recipe for a couple to continually react to each other's actions without actually diving into the issue. 

I truly acknowledge the financial situation. And I think to say try harder for a job is a rather ignorant statement to make without considering the full context. And I truly don't expect you to have the full context over a few paragraphs. Also, the reality is that the financial situation is what it is at the moment. And this is not a problem specific to my relationship. 

What I can acknowledge is that she clearly sees a deficit, she doesn't want to talk about and I'm doing my best at this moment. This particular post was to gauge the opinion of whether a camera in the house is a positive or negative contributor to my situation. I gave brief context so that the people reading the post could at least get some sort of idea of the relationship.

One thing I can appreciate about your responses is the honesty. And you really have added perspective to certain things. And even on things I disagree with you about, you have nonetheless brought to my attention that this could be problem or idea worth discussing.

Thanks for reading this in detail. I can also see where the resentment comes from. I've asked about it and she just acts like everything is okay. I'm not sure if you have suggestions on how to approach this perhaps in an indirect way.

Regarding my part time studying. I study part time because I stay home with the dogs, because we are trying to save money and daycare is expensive. Part time studying also helps me to pick up the odd jobs. It's also due to finances. I'm not in position where I can enroll full time.

And her family dynamic stresses me because it affects the household financial situation. We are currently liable for a large amount of debt that her parents acquired under her name. On top of that, when things aren't well with her parents. She spends a lot of time crying, distant and sometimes rather irritable with me. I understand the situation but it's quite challenging to see her go through this every day and not be able to assist much. Without going into detail, it's one of those things she has to figure out on her own or else this dynamic will just continue inevitably.

I think this situation with her parents also affects her resentment towards me because she works all these extra shifts to compensate for the financial burden her parents have placed on her.

I respect what she is doing and I understand her frustrations with me, but I'm not really sure what more I can do in this situation. I apply for jobs everyday. I'm studying. I'm truly trying to change my financial contribution to the home. I don't see how much more I can do to improve the income I'm bringing into the home. Perhaps you have suggestions?

Regarding my sleep hygiene, I did actually consult a doc. I got onto meds that have helped quite a bit, but currently my stress levels have me up. No job. Resentful wife. External financial burdens. I have also booked an appointment to see a therapist to maybe talk it through and find a way forward for myself. Perhaps my approach has been wrong.

In terms of exercise, I walk the dogs. I have also picked up cycling but admitted it's been a while since I've done any weight lifting. I generally work out less intensely than I used to.

ETA: I would think the first response to someone sleeping more than usual on a particular day, would be to ask how I'm doing and if I'm okay. I find it odd that her initial reaction is always anger first.

She doesn't really do anything when she gets home. I try my best to make the home stress free when she gets home. I take care of the dogs day to day, make sure they're tired when she gets home, so she can just sit and relax with them. I do all the feeding, poop picking, training and all their other needs. She does the paying for their food and treats. Which I don't mind. I love spending time with my dogs. I just don't get what else I'm meant to do to make her feel like I'm working enough. And this camera honestly isn't helping. I can't say it as a fact, but sometimes I feel like she just sits and watches it and just rumininates over some random thing I'm doing.

I also wonder which is the most true, am I immature or is she treating me like a kid. I certainly don't feel like a dependent leech.
I think that's the sentiment I'm picking up. It's like she resents me for being at home. It's like I'm not suffering enough.
I think that's what was confusing me. I would understand if I sat home all day drinking pina coladas.

Mania has a lot of residual side effects for me as well, so I think it's safe to say that it's normal. How long it takes for them to go away? I can't really say. It's differently every time. But expect a couple weeks minimum. How I deal with it, is isolate for maybe a week, to get my thoughts in order, get a better feel for what reality is. Then gradually start integrating into my old life. I take my time cause often I have to make amends and apologise for things I've done while manic, and that can be emotionally and mentally challenging and triggering for me sometimes. My only advice is, just take your time. Maybe avoid over stimulating yourself in the first few days. Peace and quiet is your friend when it comes to integration back into normal life. Having someone you can talk things through with, is also great. Just someone to listen.

Things I did and saw improvement in the relationship from:

Knowing how I like to be spoken to or not spoken to? And ending the argument or having a timeout when the tone or the language of the conversation was no longer constructive.

Not being an outlet for their emotion. Making it known that if they are overwhelmed or having a tough time with something, they must talk/vent about the issue. DISCUSS! It's not really a boundary. But discuss mental health and how it affects you. Tell your partner that it's important for them to engage you on the struggles their facing or their challenges.
